title: Geometric regularity ascends along smooth ring maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $k$-algebras which is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Assume $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Then $B$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QF (lemma-geometrically-regular-goes-up, line 47187) and its proof (Lemma 00T4 lemma-base-change-smooth, Lemma 07NF lemma-regular-goes-up); the Stacks proof runs over finitely generated field extensions (condition (1) of Lemma 0381), the definition here uses finite purely inseparable ones (condition (2)); Noetherianity of $B$: $B$ is of finite presentation over the Noetherian ring $A$ (Lemma 00FN, Hilbert basis theorem), implicit in Stacks since Definition 0382 is for Noetherian algebras

proof.text: $B$ is Noetherian. Since $\varphi$ is smooth, clause (i) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] gives $B\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ as $A$-algebras; in particular $A\to B$ is of finite type. As $A$ is Noetherian, $B$ is Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. (Stacks states 07QF without this clause because Definition 0382 is only made for Noetherian algebras; the Noetherianity is needed for $B$ to be a candidate for geometric regularity in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence, line 5991), first sentence; implicit in Lemma Tag 07QF via Definition Tag 0382

proof.text: Fix a finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ and put $A'=k'\otimes_kA$. Since $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$, the ring $A'$ is a regular ring (Noetherian, all localizations at primes regular local), by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. (Stacks lets $k'/k$ run over finitely generated field extensions, condition (1) of Lemma 0381; the definition used here is condition (2), finite purely inseparable extensions, which are finitely generated, and the argument is the same.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07QF (lemma-geometrically-regular-goes-up, line 47187) and its proof

proof.text: The ring map $\mathrm{id}_{k'}\otimes\varphi:A'=k'\otimes_kA\to k'\otimes_kB$ is smooth. By base change of smooth ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1), applied to the smooth map $A\to B$ and the ring map $A\to A'$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, the map $A'\to A'\otimes_AB$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with $R=k$, $S=A$, the $k$-algebra $k'$ and the $A$-algebra $B$ (via $\varphi$), there is an isomorphism $B\otimes_A(A\otimes_kk')\cong B\otimes_kk'$, $b\otimes(a\otimes c)\mapsto\varphi(a)b\otimes c$. Composing it with the symmetry isomorphisms of tensor products, $A'\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_A(A\otimes_kk')\to B\otimes_kk'\to k'\otimes_kB$ sends $(c\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto c\otimes\varphi(a)b$; it is a ring isomorphism, and composed with $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ it is $c\otimes a\mapsto c\otimes\varphi(a)$, i.e. it is an isomorphism of $A'$-algebras from $A'\otimes_AB$ to $k'\otimes_kB$ (with $A'$ acting through $\mathrm{id}_{k'}\otimes\varphi$). The three conditions of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] (finite presentation, $H_1(L)=0$, $\Omega$ finite projective) are invariant under isomorphism of $A'$-algebras, so $\mathrm{id}_{k'}\otimes\varphi$ is smooth (in Mathlib: Algebra.Smooth.of_equiv, RingTheory/Smooth/Basic.lean line 554).

proof.text: $k'\otimes_kB$ is a regular ring: it receives the smooth ring map $\mathrm{id}_{k'}\otimes\varphi$ of step 3 from the regular ring $A'$ of step 2, so it is Noetherian with all localizations at primes regular local by ascent of regularity along smooth ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent].

proof.text: Conclusion: $B$ is a Noetherian $k$-algebra (step 1) and $k'\otimes_kB$ is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable extension $k'/k$ (steps 2-4, $k'$ arbitrary), so $B$ is geometrically regular over $k$ by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].
